newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up, but fund selling seen.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up, but fund selling seen.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher on short-covering by commerical and speculative traders, but gave back most of the day's gains on light liquidation and switches into December, brokers said.

The market is divided over the next move of the hedge funds. The commitment of traders report appears to show the non-commercial positions net long, but the floor believes the funds are short and holding.
"I think what you have are a number of hard-core funds that are always long," said one dealer. "They're long all the way up to 120 cents. But the rest of the funds are slowly liquidating."

The active September contract reached a high of 106.60 cents before retreating late in the session to settle at 105.20 cents a lb, up 0.30 cent from Tuesday. The spot month finished at 105.00 cents a lb, up 0.30 cents. The September-Dec bakwardation narrowed 0.10 cents to 2.05 cents.
"We only expect to see a roll-over of about 10,000 lots," one dealer said. "It's not going to have much of an impact." September open interest totaled 20,891 lots at the close of business Tuesday.
Arbitrage dealers were also sellers at the top of the range, but couldn't generate much volume. "The arbitrage has been essentially flat," said one arbitrager. "There's not much going on."
The same could be said for the physical market. "It's kind of like shouting down a hole," said one physical trader. "I'm not even making any calls. It's pretty dead."

"The U.S. keeps kind of ticking along," another dealer said. "The real question is how much of European consumers' internal stocks have been liquidating during the backwardation? Is demand going to come back after August? Will the Chinese be back in the fourth quarter? These are questions that will need to be answered as we move forward."
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
